title: Count Subtrees With Max Distance Between Cities
summary: Given a tree with n cities numbered from 1 to n, where the connections between cities are represented by an array of edges, find the number of subtrees for each possible maximum distance d from 1 to n-1.
statement: Given a tree with n cities numbered from 1 to n, where the connections between cities are represented by an array of edges, find the number of subtrees for each possible maximum distance d from 1 to n-1. Here, the maximum distance between any two cities in a subtree is the longest path between them, measured by the number of edges in the path. Return an array where the d^th element represents the count of subtrees with the maximum distance of d between any two cities.
constraints: The edges form a tree on vertices 1 through n, where 2 <= n <= 15.
For every nonempty connected vertex subset with at least two vertices, compute its induced-subtree diameter in edges.
Return counts for diameters 1 through n-1.
hints: Because the full graph is a tree, an induced subset is connected exactly when it contains vertex_count-1 tree edges.
Precompute all tree distances, then enumerate vertex masks.
For connected masks, take the maximum pair distance and increment its diameter bucket.
Distances inside a connected induced subtree equal their unique full-tree path lengths because every path vertex must also be in the connected subset.
editorial: Distances inside a connected induced subtree equal their unique full-tree path lengths because every path vertex must also be in the connected subset.

tests.explanation: Three two-vertex subtrees have diameter one, and four larger connected subsets have diameter two.
The only subset containing both vertices has diameter one.
